In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Fourier–Mukai transform''' ''Φ''<sub>''K''</sub>  is a [[functor]] between [[derived category|derived categories]] of [[coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]] D(''X'') → D(''Y'') for [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]] ''X'' and ''Y'', which is, in a sense, an [[integral transform]] along a kernel object ''K'' ∈ D(''X''×''Y''). Most natural functors, including basic ones like [[direct image functor|pushforwards]] and [[inverse image functor|pullbacks]], are of this type.

These kinds of functors were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Mukai|year=1981|authorlink=Shigeru Mukai}} in order to prove an [[equivalence of categories|equivalence]] between the derived categories of coherent sheaves on an [[abelian variety]] and its [[dual abelian variety|dual]]. That equivalence is analogous to the classical [[Fourier transform]] that gives an isomorphism between [[Distribution (mathematics)|tempered distribution]]s on a finite-dimensional real [[vector space]] and its [[dual vector space|dual]].

==Definition==

Let ''X'' and ''Y'' be [[smooth scheme|smooth]] [[projective variety|projective varieties]], ''K'' ∈ D<sup>b</sup>(''X''×''Y'') an object in the derived category of coherent sheaves on their product. Denote by ''q'' the projection ''X''×''Y''→''X'', by ''p'' the projection ''X''×''Y''→''Y''. Then the Fourier-Mukai transform ''Φ''<sub>''K''</sub> is a functor D<sup>b</sup>(''X'')→D<sup>b</sup>(''Y'') given by
:<math>\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathrm{R}p_*\left(q^*\mathcal{F} \otimes^{L} K\right)</math>
where R''p''<sub>*</sub> is the [[derived functor|derived]] [[direct image functor]] and <math>\otimes^L</math> is the derived [[tensor product of modules|tensor product]].

Fourier-Mukai transforms always have left and right [[adjoint functor|adjoints]], both of which are also kernel transformations. Given two kernels ''K''<sub>1</sub> ∈ D<sup>b</sup>(''X''×''Y'') and ''K''<sub>2</sub> ∈ D<sup>b</sup>(''Y''×''Z''), the composed functor ''Φ''<sub>''K''<sub>2</sub></sub> <math>\circ</math> ''Φ''<sub>''K''<sub>1</sub></sub> is also a Fourier-Mukai transform.

The structure sheaf of the diagonal <math>\mathcal{O}_{\Delta} \in \mathrm{D}^b(X \times X)</math>, taken as a kernel, produces the identity functor on D<sup>b</sup>(''X''). For a morphism ''f'':''X''→''Y'', the structure sheaf of the graph Γ<sub>''f''</sub> produces a [[direct image functor|pushforward]] when viewed as an object in D<sup>b</sup>(''X''×''Y''), or a [[inverse image functor|pullback]] when viewed as an object in D<sup>b</sup>(''Y''×''X'').

==On abelian varieties==
Let <math>X</math> be an [[abelian variety]] and <math>\hat X</math> be its [[Dual abelian variety|dual variety]]. The [[Poincaré bundle]] <math>\mathcal P</math> on <math>X \times \hat X</math>, normalized to be trivial on the fiber at zero, can be used as a Fourier-Mukai kernel. Let <math>p</math> and <math>\hat p</math> be the canonical projections.
The corresponding Fourier–Mukai functor with kernel <math>\mathcal P</math> is then
:<math>R\mathcal S: \mathcal F \in D(X) \mapsto R\hat p_\ast (p^\ast \mathcal F \otimes \mathcal P) \in D(\hat X)</math>

There is a similar functor

:<math>R\widehat{\mathcal S} : D(\hat X) \to D(X). \, </math>

If the [[Canonical bundle|canonical class]] of a variety is [[ample line bundle|ample]] or anti-ample, then the derived category of coherent sheaves determines the variety.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Bondal | first1 = Aleksei | last2 = Orlov | first2=Dmitri | title = Reconstruction of a variety from the derived category and groups of autoequivalences | journal = Compositio Mathematica | volume = 125 | issue = 3 | pages = 327–344 | year = 2001 | doi = 10.1023/A:1002470302976 | arxiv=alg-geom/9712029  | url = http://www.mi.ras.ru/~orlov/papers/Compositio2001.pdf| doi-access = free }}</ref> In general, an abelian variety is not isomorphic to its dual, so this Fourier–Mukai transform gives examples of different varieties (with trivial canonical bundles) that have equivalent derived categories. 

Let ''g'' denote the dimension of ''X''. The Fourier–Mukai transformation is nearly involutive :
:<math>R\mathcal S \circ R\widehat{\mathcal S} = (-1)^\ast [-g]</math>

It interchanges [[Pontryagin product|Pontrjagin product]] and [[tensor product]].
:<math>R\mathcal S(\mathcal F \ast \mathcal G)  = R\mathcal S(\mathcal F) \otimes R\mathcal S(\mathcal G)</math>
:<math>R\mathcal S(\mathcal F \otimes \mathcal G)  = R\mathcal S(\mathcal F) \ast R\mathcal S(\mathcal G)[g]</math>

{{harvtxt|Deninger|Murre|1991}} have used the Fourier-Mukai transform to prove the [[Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles|Künneth decomposition]] for the [[Chow motive]]s of abelian varieties.

==Applications in string theory==

In [[string theory]], [[T-duality]] (short for ''target space duality''), which relates two [[quantum field theories]] or string theories with different spacetime geometries, is closely related with the Fourier-Mukai transformation.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Leung | first1 = Naichung Conan | last2 = Yau | first2 = Shing-Tung |author-link2=Shing-Tung Yau | last3 = Zaslow | first3 = Eric |author-link3=Eric Zaslow | title = From special Lagrangian to Hermitian-Yang-Mills via Fourier-Mukai transform | journal = Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics | volume = 4 | issue = 6 | pages = 1319–1341 | year = 2000 | doi = 10.4310/ATMP.2000.v4.n6.a5 | url = http://intlpress.com/site/pub/pages/journals/items/atmp/content/vols/0004/0006/a005/index.html| arxiv = math/0005118 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gevorgyan | first1 = Eva | last2 = Sarkissian | first2 = Gor | title = Defects, non-abelian t-duality, and the Fourier-Mukai transform of the Ramond-Ramond fields | journal = Journal of High Energy Physics | volume = 2014 | issue = 3 | pages = 35 | year = 2014 | doi = 10.1007/JHEP03(2014)035 | arxiv = 1310.1264 }}</ref>
